caption:
Six pallets of Nvidia hardware, reportedly worth $11.4 million, left Oakland on August 29 for Fort Worth, Texas.
They never arrived. Investigators lost the truck in San Bernardino County.
Oakland police are investigating a grand theft, and no arrests have been announced.

Who do you think ends up with stolen AI hardware like this?

paragraphs.text: A shipment of Nvidia hardware reportedly worth $11.4 million disappeared on its way from Oakland, California, to Fort Worth, Texas, according to reports by KTVU and ABC7 News published on November 6, 2026. The load consisted of six pallets of Nvidia hardware and was collected in Oakland on August 29.

The cargo never reached Fort Worth. Investigators lost track of the truck and its drivers in San Bernardino County, according to KTVU, which based its report on a review of court records by reporter Henry Lee.
How the load was picked up

Authorities told ABC7 News that the pickup itself went as planned and that the truck that collected the cargo was identified as belonging to a food transport company. FreightWaves, citing The Mercury News, reported that the vehicle displayed a food transportation company's logo when it arrived.

According to FreightWaves, investigators tracked the truck through several long stops, some lasting multiple hours, before losing its trail in Southern California. The outlet noted that investigators have not publicly explained those stops and have not said whether criminals posed as a legitimate transportation provider.

The Oakland Police Department said in a statement that it is investigating a grand theft that occurred in East Oakland. The victim reported the crime on September 13, 2026, about two weeks after the pickup. No arrests or recoveries have been announced.

FreightWaves reported that police have not confirmed the $11.4 million value or described the exact merchandise, and that the shipper, carrier and driver have not been publicly identified. The outlet said it contacted Nvidia for comment and had not received a response.
A pattern of Nvidia cargo crime

The case is not the first involving Nvidia products in the Bay Area. In 2025, police in Fremont and Union City investigated burglaries of Nvidia cargo valued at more than $7.5 million. In September 2026, thieves apparently targeted trucks they believed carried Nvidia technology, but the trailers held about 40,000 pounds of sand. No link between those cases and the Oakland theft has been established.

Olaf Groth of the UC Berkeley Haas School of Business told ABC7 News that the chips sell for about double their US price elsewhere, giving thieves strong incentives wherever security is weak. He called the hardware a national security asset and said it is a concern because nobody knows where such chips end up. KTVU also reported that nearly 700 cargo thefts were recorded across the US and Canada in the second quarter of the year.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the case shows how the value of AI hardware has turned ordinary freight into a high value target. A single truckload can carry millions of dollars in chips, yet it moves through the same pickups and highway stops as any other freight. The reported use of a food company's branding points to how thieves can exploit trust in routine pickups.

The next thing to watch is whether Oakland police or federal investigators identify the carrier that collected the load and link the theft to the wider string of chip and electronics heists in California.
